summary: Round-1 Tier-2 closing review of aWindowedPass (886b089...e252baf). Verdict: BLOCKED. The tally is 22 items (1 blocker, 3 high, 12 medium, 6 low), or 27 raw confirmed findings (2/4/15/6). The blocker is that memory-tree's unconditional {memory_root}/backlog [[generated]] rows collide with the default and example SHARED_RECORDS, so an adopter's driver exits 2 on every verb. The skeptic-corrected fix is a `when = BACKLOG_MODE=builds` condition on those rows. The same defect is bound high as id 10, whose sound-judged fix conflicts with that correction; the report flags the conflict. The highs are vacuous check-23 negative arms (ids 13 and 14) and --check-commit's rename detection (id 23). The run was complete: 5/5 lenses and 5/5 skeptic batches returned. No specs or context were supplied, and no checklist was swept.

ledger.reason: At e252baf, resolve_generated_indexes lists the tracked tools/*/kit.toml files with ls-files, then awk-reads each one from the working tree ($_rg_root/$_rg_d). Check 23 (check_generated_render) and verb_check_commit both forgive any path a resolved row covers. So a pass that may write tools/foo/kit.toml can add a broad [[generated]] row, for example path="tools" with generator set to a file the kit already ships, and its own and its siblings' writes go uncounted. govkit 6c checks only the tokens, that the generator exists and that why is non-empty, so it accepts the row. The diff did make this route reachable. The class is not new, though: at base GENERATED_INDEXES came from the working-tree .unattended.conf, which a pass could edit the same way to exempt itself. The diff adds a parallel route rather than a new capability, and it needs a deliberately broad row. Contained, so medium.
ledger.claim: resolve_generated_indexes reads the exemption list from every tracked tools/*/kit.toml in the working tree at grading time. A pass can write that file inside its own declared kit and so exempt any path from check 23 and from --check-commit.

ledger.reason: In pass_commit, a commit with any Pass: trailer is attributed only by that trailer: case " none " does not contain the unit, so the loop continues. A Pass: none commit is therefore never a unit's pass commit, and check 23 never subset-tests it. If no commit names the pass, the dodged-join branch only printfs. So the comment at unattended.sh 9704-9705 ("`Pass: none` is taken at its word. Check 23 still grades both at the close") is false for Pass: none, and so is the commit-msg hook's line-48 fallback wording when it reaches a Pass: none commit. The behaviour itself is by design: TOOL-aWindowedPass-2 says Pass: none names no unit. It is also equivalent to the base, where a commit whose subject did not name the unit was equally ungraded. The defect is a misstated backstop in comments, with no change in behaviour.
ledger.claim: verb_check_commit and the commit-msg hook (lines 35 and 48) say that check 23 "still grades" a `Pass: none` commit at the close. It does not: pass_commit (lib-unattended.sh:736) attributes a `Pass: none` commit to no unit, so the subset test never sees its paths.

ledger.reason: verb_check_commit builds trl with `git interpret-trailers --parse | sed -n 's/^Pass: *//p'`, which is case-sensitive. I confirmed on git 2.54 that --parse keeps a lowercase `pass:` key as written. git log's %(trailers:key=Pass), which pass_commit and log_attribution_tokens use, matches the key case-insensitively. A message trailed `pass: TOOL-x-1` with a subject that does not name the unit therefore returns 0 from the hook, yet the close attributes it to TOOL-x-1 and grades it. Separately, `case " $trl " in *" none "*) return 0` short-circuits on any none token, while pass_commit attributes `TOOL-x-1 none` to TOOL-x-1. The commit-time step and the close disagree. The close still catches the write, as it did before this diff, but only once the declaration can no longer be widened. Contained, so medium.
ledger.claim: The commit-time step parses the Pass trailer differently from the close. Its sed `^Pass:` is case-sensitive, while git log's `%(trailers:key=Pass)` is case-insensitive. And any `none` token in the trailer short-circuits the whole check at line 9730, while pass_commit still attributes the commit to the other ids it names.

ledger.reason: At e252baf, tools/memory-tree/kit.toml declares {memory_root}/backlog as [[generated]] with no condition, in two rows. The resolver reads tools/*/kit.toml beside the unattended kit, and the comment says adopters read the same descriptors. The shipped .unattended.conf.example still sets SHARED_RECORDS="memory/DECISIONS.md memory/backlog", and the resolve_shared_records default is "$2/DECISIONS.md $2/backlog". scan_shared_index_overlaps then reports memory/backlog under both keys. unattended.sh refuses at load with exit 2 on every verb, and check 38 fails. Gov's own conf escapes only because its SHARED_RECORDS omits backlog. The repo's later fix (the closing review r1 B1 comment and test arm) states that every adopter's conf was refused at load.
ledger.claim: The memory-tree kit.toml now declares `{memory_root}/backlog` as a [[generated]] output (two rows: gen_build_index.py and backlog.py). But the shipped example conf still sets `SHARED_RECORDS="memory/DECISIONS.md memory/backlog"`, and the kit default for an undeclared key (`resolve_shared_records` in lib-unattended.sh, `$2/DECISIONS.md $2/backlog`) names it too. So once `resolve_generated_indexes` merges the kit rows, `scan_shared_index_overlaps` reports `memory/backlog` under both keys.

ledger.reason: verb_check_commit collects staged paths with porcelain `git diff --cached --name-only`, which applies diff.renames (default true) and lists only the destination of a staged rename. Check 23 grades the commit with `diff-tree --no-commit-id --name-only -r`, which detects no renames and lists both the deleted source and the new path. If a pass runs `git mv` on an undeclared file into a declared directory, the hook sees only the declared destination and passes. At the close, check 23 counts the deleted source as an undeclared write, after --dispatch can no longer widen the declaration. The scenario is real but narrow, and the close still catches it, so medium.
ledger.claim: `--check-commit` collects staged paths with porcelain `git diff --cached --name-only`, which detects renames by default (diff.renames=true) and lists only the new name. Check 23 grades the same commit with `diff-tree --name-only -r`, which does no rename detection and lists both the deleted old path and the new one. The commit-time copy of the rule and the close-time copy therefore see different path sets.

ledger.reason: During `git commit --amend` of a pass commit, HEAD is that pass commit when commit-msg runs. check_pass_open calls pass_commit over anchor..HEAD, which finds HEAD with the Pass: u trailer and declared writes, so it returns 1 (closed). rows then omits u, decl is empty, and verb_check_commit refuses with 'has no open dispatched pass ... declare it first'. The refusal blocks an ordinary amend. Following the printed --dispatch remedy anchors a row at a commit the amend then orphans, and switching to Pass: none drops the attribution. --no-verify is the workaround. The effect is a contained false refusal, so medium.
ledger.claim: `--check-commit` only accepts a `Pass: <unit>` trailer for a unit with an OPEN row. When `git commit --amend` is run on a pass commit, HEAD is that pass commit, so `pass_commit`/`check_pass_open` call the pass closed and the hook refuses with 'has no open dispatched pass ... declare it first'.

ledger.reason: At e252baf, check 23 reads the pass commit's subject with `dshitsub=$(GIT log -1 --format=%s "$dshit")` and runs `id_in "$dshitsub" "$dssunit"` on each sibling. In the same diff, `pass_commit` was changed to attribute a commit by its `Pass:` trailer alone when one is present. Before this diff both sides read the subject, so a subject naming two siblings really was ambiguous. Now a commit with `Pass: X-3` and a subject that mentions X-2 is selected only for X-3, yet the guard still prints 'one commit names two passes' and `continue`s, so that pass's undeclared writes are never graded. The reverse case also holds. `--check-commit` accepts a multi-id trailer, and `pass_commit` would select a `Pass: A B` commit for both A and B. The guard misses it unless the subject names both, so each unit is graded against the other's writes. I grade this medium: the path is narrow, and the refusal line goes to the default channel instead of failing silently.
ledger.claim: Check 23's ambiguous-attribution test still reads only the pass commit's subject (`%s`) and tests it against sibling units with `id_in`. After TOOL-aWindowedPass-2, however, `pass_commit` attributes a commit that has a `Pass:` trailer by the trailer alone and never reads its subject.

ledger.reason: `verb_check_commit` does `git interpret-trailers --parse <msg | sed -n 's/^Pass: *//p'`, which is case-sensitive, and `--parse` keeps the key's case as written. `pass_commit` and `log_attribution_tokens` use `%(trailers:key=Pass)`, which git matches case-insensitively. So a `pass: X` trailer is ignored by the hook but still attributes the commit at the close. The effect is limited. Either the hook asks for a trailer that is already there, and fixing the case clears it, or the staged-path check is skipped and check 23 still grades the pass at the close.
ledger.claim: `--check-commit` pulls trailers with a case-sensitive `sed 's/^Pass: *//p'`. The attribution side (`%(trailers:key=Pass)` in `pass_commit` and `log_attribution_tokens`) matches the key case-insensitively.

ledger.reason: At e252baf, tools/memory-tree/kit.toml declares two `[[generated]]` rows with path `{memory_root}/backlog`. `resolve_generated_indexes` reads every tracked `kit.toml` beside the unattended kit, so this is what an adopter gets as well. Right after both resolve, unattended.sh calls `scan_shared_index_overlaps`, prints REFUSING and does `exit 2` before any verb dispatches, `--check-commit` included. Check 38 in check-unattended.sh reports the same overlap. Before this diff the example's GENERATED_INDEXES did not name backlog, so the diff introduced the conflict. Gov's own bar stays green only because gov's .unattended.conf no longer lists backlog under SHARED_RECORDS. I grade this high, not blocker. It fails closed with a message naming the remedy, and it does not produce a wrong result or certify an unchecked change. It still blocks every verb for an adopter on the default or example value.

ledger.reason: Duplicate of finding 9: the misplaced build_commit header and the `log_attribution_tokens` / `GEN_REGION_AWK` blocks inserted above it are the third part of finding 9, and that finding is confirmed.

ledger.reason: At e252baf the only thing that prints 'check 23 FAILED' is `fail 23` (check-unattended.sh:3897). It runs only when ds_over_n>0 and the record's run-branch/branch-ref equals DS_HEAD_REF. The PRISTINE tRun RUN.md has no run-branch or branch-ref fact; only `bindrun` adds one. With a single unit, dsposok=2, so dsov=0 and any undeclared write prints a SOLO line rather than being counted. With no base, a counted write in an unbound run prints OTHER RUN. So every cited arm (3466, 3602, 3633, 3672, 3714, 3774, 3842) that uses drow/drows with a single unit and no bindrun, followed by `miss "check 23 FAILED"`, cannot fail. F's second miss at 3658 has two units but is unbound, so it gets OTHER RUN at most. Its first miss, the ambiguity text, is still effective. At base the fixture's UNDECLARED_WRITE_CEILING was 0, so these arms could fire there. This diff made them vacuous, so it is in scope. Production code is unaffected today, but regressions to covers, the fold or the windowing would go undetected. That misleads the next change, so high.
ledger.claim: Most negative check-23 arms are now vacuous. They dispatch one unit through plain `drow` on a record with no run-branch, then assert only `miss "check 23 FAILED"`. After 7ab7ae535/c5582706e that pair of conditions can never print FAILED: a single-unit run is always SOLO, and an unbound run prints OTHER RUN.

ledger.reason: The arm (check-unattended.test.sh ~3719-3725 at e252baf) is drow ARCH-tRun-1 (single unit, unbound) followed by `miss "check 23 FAILED"`. If pass_commit's `[ -n "$_ptr" ]` branch (lib-unattended.sh:736-738) were removed, id_in would match the 'records for ARCH-tRun-1..3' subject; the spec comment itself says a range like -1..4 was taken as the pass. The records commit would then be graded and print SOLO with notes/records.md, never FAILED. The no-trailer sibling arm only hits 'ARCH-tRun-1 at', and the build_commit arm exercises log_attribution_tokens, not pass_commit. git grep finds no other test that drives pass_commit with a `Pass: none` commit. unattended.test.sh only feeds message files to --check-commit. So nothing that can fail covers the trailer attribution in pass_commit.
ledger.claim: The only arm for pass_commit's new `Pass:` trailer attribution (TOOL-aWindowedPass-2) cannot fail. It uses a single-unit, unbound `drow` and asserts `miss "check 23 FAILED"`. If the trailer were ignored and the `records for ARCH-tRun-1..3` commit were taken as the pass, its notes/records.md write would print SOLO, not FAILED.

ledger.reason: At e252baf, arm B is `reset_tree; drows ARCH-tRun-1 ...; drow ARCH-tRun-9 ...` with no bindrun. reset_tree restores PRISTINE, whose RUN.md Run facts hold only phase, witness and base. The overlap is counted (ds_over_n=1), but dsrb is empty while DS_HEAD_REF is refs/heads/unit. The checker therefore prints 'check 23 OTHER RUN ...', and the fail-23 text the arm hits ('a pass of the run this branch drives ...') is never printed, so the arm is red. The diff introduced this: it changed the hit text and added the sibling row but not bindrun. The production grading itself is correct. The effect is a red arm and an unobserved property, which is contained, so medium.
ledger.claim: Widening arm B asserts the bound-run failure text, but its fixture never binds the run. It runs `reset_tree; drows ...; drow ARCH-tRun-9` with no `bindrun`, and the PRISTINE RUN.md has no run-branch or branch-ref fact. So check 23 prints `check 23 OTHER RUN`, never the `fail 23` message, and the arm is red at e252baf.

ledger.reason: At e252baf, check-brief-recorded.sh fills _SUBJ from `done < <(log_attribution_tokens HEAD)` (line 303) and holds no `| tr -c`; the pipeline now lives in lib-unattended.sh's log_attribution_tokens. ledger.claim: The truncated-subject-cache arm stages its break with `sed 's#| tr -c#| head -n -1 | tr -c#'` on the copied leg. 55213dd2f moved that pipeline into lib-unattended.sh's log_attribution_tokens, so the leg no longer contains `| tr -c`. The sed is a no-op and the arm's expected rc 2 cannot happen.

ledger.reason: The shipped .unattended.conf.example at e252baf sets GENERATED_INDEXES="" (line 378); at base it carried the {{MEMORY_TREE_DIR}} pair. Arm 10 in adopt-unattended.test.sh still expects the stamped pair, so the stamp leaves the line empty and the `same` assertion reds. The diff made this reachable.
ledger.claim: Adopter arm 10 still expects the stamped example to carry `GENERATED_INDEXES="memory/LIVE.md:...gen_build_index.py memory/ledger:..."`. 75cd13f71 changed the shipped .unattended.conf.example to `GENERATED_INDEXES=""`.

ledger.reason: The diff adds an --check-commit block to .githooks/commit-msg (lines 31-51) ahead of the MERGE_HEAD exit. The only behavioural test of the hook is transition-audit.test.sh F10. F10's new_repo fixture has no unattended kit and no .unattended.conf, so the new block is skipped there. check-wiring.test.sh writes a stub hook, and unattended.test.sh calls --check-commit directly. Spec AC5 is only a grep for 'check-commit'. Moving the call below the merge-only exit, mis-mapping rc, or breaking the kit/conf probe would leave every suite green. The effect is contained: check 23 still grades at the close. So medium.
ledger.claim: The hook's new behaviour has no arm. It now runs on every commit ahead of the MERGE_HEAD exit, probes for the kit and conf, blocks only on `rc = 1`, and announces and passes on any other exit code. unattended.test.sh calls `--check-commit` directly, and check-wiring.test.sh only byte-compares a stub commit-msg.

ledger.reason: At e252baf, check-unattended.sh sets dsposok=0 when the base does not resolve, and every pass is then counted as overlapped (dsov=1). No test file at e252baf asserts 'check 23 overlap unavailable' or 'counted as overlapped'. The base-0000 fixtures at test lines 1419 and 1792 only assert the separate BASE-resolve check. The fail-closed arm is therefore unguarded. A later commit (e4abc55bf, 'M7') adds exactly this arm, which confirms the gap was real. The effect is contained to test coverage.
ledger.claim: The fail-closed path of overlap placement has no arm. When the record's base does not resolve (dsposok=0), every graded pass is counted as overlapped and the `check 23 overlap unavailable` line is reported. No fixture sets an unresolvable base.

ledger.reason: The --check-commit block in unattended.test.sh (lines 5742-5779 at e252baf) covers four cases: an undeclared stray path, run-state plus a conf GENERATED_INDEXES subtraction, a subject with no trailer, Pass: none, and an unbound branch. Nothing stages a brief row, which would exercise read_brief_paths with an empty commit, i.e. the index. Nothing stages a gen-region-only edit, which would exercise check_gen_region_only HEAD:$p :$p. Nothing sends a trailer naming a unit with no open dispatch row. Those three branches are reachable and untested. The effect is limited to verification.
ledger.claim: Three of verb_check_commit's branches have no arm: the brief-row subtraction (read_brief_paths over the index), the gen-region-only subtraction (`check_gen_region_only "HEAD:$p" ":$p"` at 9761), and the refusal when the trailer names a unit with no open pass (9749). The AC3 arm covers only the run-state file and a conf-declared generated output.

ledger.reason: 6c ORs together missing path, missing generator, extra tokens, missing generator file and missing why into one failure. The only selftest arm added (aWP-4 AC5) swaps the generator for a missing file. A regression in the token-set comparison or in the why test would leave selftest green. This is a test gap only, with no runtime effect.
ledger.claim: Selfcheck 6c's only arm stages a missing generator. Its other failure conditions are never staged: a path token outside {memory_root,map_root,kit}, an empty path, and a missing `why`.

ledger.reason: At e252baf, memory-tree/kit.toml declares two unconditional [[generated]] rows for {memory_root}/backlog. resolve_generated_indexes reads every tools/*/kit.toml with no condition support. resolve_shared_records defaults an undeclared key to '$M/DECISIONS.md $M/backlog', and .unattended.conf.example sets SHARED_RECORDS="memory/DECISIONS.md memory/backlog". So scan_shared_index_overlaps finds memory/backlog under both keys. unattended.sh then exits 2 at conf load for every verb, and check 38 reds. Gov escapes only because its own conf removed backlog from SHARED_RECORDS. The later fix commit e4abc55bf names this B1 and adds `when = ".memory-tree.conf:BACKLOG_MODE=builds"`.
ledger.claim: memory-tree declares two `{memory_root}/backlog` [[generated]] rows with no condition. The kit's default SHARED_RECORDS (`resolve_shared_records`) and the shipped `.unattended.conf.example` both put `memory/backlog` under SHARED_RECORDS, so every adopter that has memory-tree installed now names one path under both condition-3 keys.

ledger.reason: verb_check_commit at e252baf reads the staged set with porcelain `git diff --cached --name-only`. diff.renames defaults to true, so a staged rename lists only its destination. Check 23 lists the commit with plumbing `git diff-tree --no-commit-id --name-only -r`, which does no rename detection and lists the deleted source too. Example: a `git mv` of an undeclared path into a declared one passes --check-commit, then is counted at close, when it can no longer be repaired. That is narrow, but it is a commit-time check certifying a commit the close grader then rejects. The later fix commit states '--check-commit lists staged paths with no rename detection'.
ledger.claim: `--check-commit` reads the staged set with porcelain `git diff --cached --name-only`, which applies rename detection (diff.renames defaults to true) and lists only a rename's destination. Check 23 at the close reads `git diff-tree --name-only -r`, which does no rename detection and lists both source and destination.

ledger.reason: At e252baf, check 23 sets dshitsub with `git log -1 --format=%s` and runs id_in over sibling ids for every pass commit, trailered or not. Spec 2 S2 (lines 30-31) says a commit with a trailer is attributed by that trailer alone and its subject is never read. pass_commit/log_attribution_tokens already honour that, so a sibling mentioned only in a trailered commit's subject cannot be selected for that sibling. The ambiguity refusal is a false positive. It prints to stdout and `continue`s, so that pass's undeclared writes are neither counted nor reported SOLO. The later fix commit states 'Check 23's ambiguity test reads a trailered commit's trailer'. The escape is contained to one pass's grading.
ledger.claim: Check 23's ambiguous-attribution test still reads the pass commit's SUBJECT (`git log -1 --format=%s`) and matches sibling unit ids in it, even when the commit carries a `Pass:` trailer. Spec 2 S2 says a trailered commit is attributed by its trailer alone and its subject is never read.

ledger.reason: In unattended.sh at e252baf, verb_check_commit reads the trailer with `sed -n 's/^Pass: *//p'`, which is case-sensitive. It reads the subject with `sed -n '/[^[:space:]]/{p;q}'`, which takes the first non-blank line only. pass_commit (lib-unattended.sh:778) and the attribution log (lib:830, check-unattended:3807) use `%s` and `%(trailers:key=Pass)`; git matches that trailer key case-insensitively, and `%s` joins the whole first paragraph. Take a commit trailered `pass: X`, or one with the unit id on a wrapped subject line and no trailer. --check-commit sees no trailer and no unit in the subject, so it exits 0, while the close attributes the commit to the pass and counts the stray write. The later fix commit on HEAD ("READ AS THE CLOSE READS THEM (closing review r1, M2/L2)") confirms the defect existed in this range. The impact is contained: check 23 still grades the commit, only the early repair is lost.
ledger.claim: `--check-commit` reads the trailer and subject differently from the close. It matches `^Pass:` case-sensitively, while `pass_commit`/`log_attribution_tokens` use `%(trailers:key=Pass)`, which is case-insensitive. It takes the subject as the first non-blank line, while the close's `%s` joins the whole first paragraph.

ledger.reason: `git commit --amend` runs commit-msg and keeps the `Pass: <unit>` trailer. During the amend HEAD is the pass commit, so pass_commit returns it, and check_pass_open sees it writing inside the declared set and returns 1 (closed). The rows list then has no entry for the unit, decl is empty, and the verb fails 49 with 'has no open dispatched pass ... declare it first: --dispatch'. An ordinary amend is therefore refused unless --no-verify is used. HEAD later added exactly the proposed 'O' row arm (closing review r1, M4), which confirms the defect was in this range.
ledger.claim: Once a pass has committed, `check_pass_open` reports its row closed. So `git commit --amend` of the pass commit, carrying its `Pass: <unit>` trailer, is refused with 'has no open dispatched pass … declare it first: --dispatch'.

ledger.reason: At e252baf, check 23 sets dsrb from the run-branch fact, falling back to branch-ref. A live record can carry neither: run-branch is not written on a detached preflight, branch-ref is written only on the second anchor, and older records predate fact 13. Such a record is reachable in this tree: memory/builds/aCollapsedScan/RUN.md is in phase LANDING with no branch fact. For it, `[ "$dsrb" = "$DS_HEAD_REF" ]` can never hold on any checkout, so the record always prints 'OTHER RUN ... graded at its own close', and that close never happens. This diff introduced the problem: before it, the repo-global ceiling counted these writes. The header comment admits that an undriven run is not failed, but the printed line still claims a later grading that never comes.
ledger.claim: A live record with neither a `run-branch` nor a `branch-ref` fact (`dsrb` empty) falls into the OTHER RUN branch. That branch prints that its counted writes are 'graded at its own close', but no checkout can ever bind an empty branch, so no close will grade them.

ledger.reason: In the commit-msg hook, the unattended probe loop runs the kit only when both unattended.sh and .unattended.conf are found, and otherwise falls through silently. It prints only when the kit ran and exited with something other than 0 or 1. Spec 3 S4 and §5 promise that an absent kit is an announced skip. When the conf is present and the kit is missing, nothing is printed. Check 23 still grades at the close, so the effect is contained.
ledger.claim: Spec 3 S4/§5 say an absent kit is an ANNOUNCED skip. When `.unattended.conf` exists but `unattended.sh` is not found, the hook's probe loop matches nothing and the commit-time check is skipped silently.

ledger.reason: Spec 4 §5 promises that check 23 prints the effective set it read, with each pair's source, and that the kit README describes the declaration. At e252baf, check-unattended.sh calls resolve_generated_indexes at line 303 and never reports the result. It only reports individual exclusions at about line 3812, which partly covers observability. The README diff adds only the hook paragraph, with no `[[generated]]` description; the PROTOCOL key row and the conf example do describe it. This is observability and docs only.
ledger.claim: Spec 4 §5 promises that check 23 prints the effective generated set on the report channel, and that the kit README describes the `[[generated]]` declaration. Neither was built: no reader reports the resolver's output, and the README diff adds only the hook line.

confirmedFindings.claim: resolve_generated_indexes reads the exemption list from every tracked tools/*/kit.toml in the working tree at grading time. A pass can write that file inside its own declared kit and so exempt any path from check 23 and from --check-commit.
confirmedFindings.fix: Make check 23 and --check-commit both resolve the kit [[generated]] rows from the run's recorded base commit (`git show <base>:<kit.toml>`), so rows added during a run never exempt that run's own writes. Fall back to the conf pairs alone when the base does not resolve. In govkit 6c, refuse a row whose resolved path is a bare root ({memory_root}, {map_root}, {kit}, a top-level directory) or covers any kit.toml or generator source.

confirmedFindings.claim: verb_check_commit and the commit-msg hook (lines 35 and 48) say that check 23 "still grades" a `Pass: none` commit at the close. It does not: pass_commit (lib-unattended.sh:736) attributes a `Pass: none` commit to no unit, so the subset test never sees its paths.
confirmedFindings.fix: Correct the verb_check_commit header and the commit-msg hook text (lines 35 and 48) to say that check 23 does not grade a Pass: none commit, and that only the non-failing dodged-join line observes declared paths moving without an attributed pass commit.

confirmedFindings.claim: The commit-time step parses the Pass trailer differently from the close. Its sed `^Pass:` is case-sensitive, while git log's `%(trailers:key=Pass)` is case-insensitive. And any `none` token in the trailer short-circuits the whole check at line 9730, while pass_commit still attributes the commit to the other ids it names.
confirmedFindings.fix: Derive trl with the parser the close uses: `git interpret-trailers --parse` with a case-insensitive key match (`sed -n 's/^[Pp][Aa][Ss][Ss]: *//p'`), or `git -c trailer.separators=: interpret-trailers --only-trailers` filtered case-insensitively. Return 0 only when `none` is the sole Pass value. Otherwise grade every non-`none` id.

confirmedFindings.claim: The memory-tree kit.toml now declares `{memory_root}/backlog` as a [[generated]] output (two rows: gen_build_index.py and backlog.py). But the shipped example conf still sets `SHARED_RECORDS="memory/DECISIONS.md memory/backlog"`, and the kit default for an undeclared key (`resolve_shared_records` in lib-unattended.sh, `$2/DECISIONS.md $2/backlog`) names it too. So once `resolve_generated_indexes` merges the kit rows, `scan_shared_index_overlaps` reports `memory/backlog` under both keys.
confirmedFindings.fix: Keep memory/backlog in SHARED_RECORDS (both the default and the example). Make the two backlog [[generated]] rows conditional on BACKLOG_MODE=builds, for example with a `when = ".memory-tree.conf:BACKLOG_MODE=builds"` key that resolve_generated_indexes evaluates. Add a suite arm that loads the example conf and the kit default against every real kit.toml and asserts no overlap, plus a builds-mode control.

confirmedFindings.claim: `--check-commit` collects staged paths with porcelain `git diff --cached --name-only`, which detects renames by default (diff.renames=true) and lists only the new name. Check 23 grades the same commit with `diff-tree --name-only -r`, which does no rename detection and lists both the deleted old path and the new one. The commit-time copy of the rule and the close-time copy therefore see different path sets.
confirmedFindings.fix: Use `git diff --cached --no-renames --name-only` (or `git diff-index --cached --name-only HEAD`) so the hook sees the same population that check 23's diff-tree sees.

confirmedFindings.claim: `--check-commit` only accepts a `Pass: <unit>` trailer for a unit with an OPEN row. When `git commit --amend` is run on a pass commit, HEAD is that pass commit, so `pass_commit`/`check_pass_open` call the pass closed and the hook refuses with 'has no open dispatched pass ... declare it first'.
confirmedFindings.fix: Detect an amend (for example, HEAD's own Pass trailer names u and the pass_commit for u's row is HEAD) and grade the index against HEAD^ using that row's declaration instead of refusing. Alternatively, evaluate openness over `<anchor>..HEAD^` when HEAD is u's pass commit.

confirmedFindings.claim: Check 23's ambiguous-attribution test still reads only the pass commit's subject (`%s`) and tests it against sibling units with `id_in`. After TOOL-aWindowedPass-2, however, `pass_commit` attributes a commit that has a `Pass:` trailer by the trailer alone and never reads its subject.
confirmedFindings.fix: Derive the ambiguity test from the same attribution source: read the commit's tokens through `log_attribution_tokens -1 "$dshit"` (the trailer ids when present, otherwise the subject) and test the siblings against those tokens.

confirmedFindings.claim: `--check-commit` pulls trailers with a case-sensitive `sed 's/^Pass: *//p'`. The attribution side (`%(trailers:key=Pass)` in `pass_commit` and `log_attribution_tokens`) matches the key case-insensitively.
confirmedFindings.fix: Match the key case-insensitively, e.g. `sed -n 's/^[Pp][Aa][Ss][Ss]: *//p'`, or read `git interpret-trailers --parse` output with an `awk` that uses `tolower` on the key.

confirmedFindings.claim: Several comments and one message still describe the retired ceiling. The comment at this line says 'the ratchet below decides the verdict'. The EXCLUDED message at line 3682 says records are 'not graded against the ceiling'. In lib-unattended.sh, the new log_attribution_tokens and GEN_REGION_AWK doc blocks were inserted between build_commit's header comment and build_commit itself, so that header now sits above unrelated functions.
confirmedFindings.fix: Reword the check 23 comment at line 3871 and the EXCLUDED message to describe per-run grading against zero. In lib-unattended.sh, keep the gen-region comment, `GEN_REGION_AWK` and `check_gen_region_only` together. Put the `log_attribution_tokens` comment directly above `log_attribution_tokens()`, and put the whole build_commit header comment directly above `build_commit()`.

confirmedFindings.claim: The new memory-tree `[[generated]]` rows declare `{memory_root}/backlog`, but the shipped example conf (`SHARED_RECORDS="memory/DECISIONS.md memory/backlog"`, .unattended.conf.example:377) and the kit default for an undeclared SHARED_RECORDS (`resolve_shared_records` prints `$M/DECISIONS.md $M/backlog`, lib-unattended.sh:508) both still name `memory/backlog` as a shared record.
confirmedFindings.fix: Drop `backlog` from the kit default in `resolve_shared_records` and from the example's SHARED_RECORDS, since it is now a generated output. Add a suite arm that copies every real `tools/*/kit.toml` into a fixture and asserts `scan_shared_index_overlaps` is empty for both the kit default and the example's value.

confirmedFindings.claim: Most negative check-23 arms are now vacuous. They dispatch one unit through plain `drow` on a record with no run-branch, then assert only `miss "check 23 FAILED"`. After 7ab7ae535/c5582706e that pair of conditions can never print FAILED: a single-unit run is always SOLO, and an unbound run prints OTHER RUN.
confirmedFindings.fix: Dispatch each negative arm through `odrow` (bound run plus an overlapping sibling), or make the negative assertion one that can still fire, e.g. `miss "$out" "wrote <path>"` / `miss "$out" "check 23 SOLO"`. Add a self-scan that reds any `miss ... check 23 FAILED` arm whose fixture neither binds the run nor dispatches a sibling.

confirmedFindings.claim: The only arm for pass_commit's new `Pass:` trailer attribution (TOOL-aWindowedPass-2) cannot fail. It uses a single-unit, unbound `drow` and asserts `miss "check 23 FAILED"`. If the trailer were ignored and the `records for ARCH-tRun-1..3` commit were taken as the pass, its notes/records.md write would print SOLO, not FAILED.
confirmedFindings.fix: Bind the run and add a sibling (`odrow`), or assert `miss "$(GOV_UNATTENDED_REPORT=1 bash "$SCRIPT" 2>&1)" "wrote notes/records.md"`. Watch it go red with the `[ -n "$_ptr" ]` branch removed.

confirmedFindings.claim: Widening arm B asserts the bound-run failure text, but its fixture never binds the run. It runs `reset_tree; drows ...; drow ARCH-tRun-9` with no `bindrun`, and the PRISTINE RUN.md has no run-branch or branch-ref fact. So check 23 prints `check 23 OTHER RUN`, never the `fail 23` message, and the arm is red at e252baf.
confirmedFindings.fix: Add `bindrun` after `reset_tree` in arm B, as `odrow` does, and confirm the arm goes green, then red with the supersede fold broken.

confirmedFindings.claim: The truncated-subject-cache arm stages its break with `sed 's#| tr -c#| head -n -1 | tr -c#'` on the copied leg. 55213dd2f moved that pipeline into lib-unattended.sh's log_attribution_tokens, so the leg no longer contains `| tr -c`. The sed is a no-op and the arm's expected rc 2 cannot happen.
confirmedFindings.fix: Truncate the leg's feed instead, e.g. rewrite `done < <(log_attribution_tokens HEAD)` to `... | head -n -1`. Assert that the sed changed the file (grep the edited line) before asserting rc 2.

confirmedFindings.claim: Adopter arm 10 still expects the stamped example to carry `GENERATED_INDEXES="memory/LIVE.md:...gen_build_index.py memory/ledger:..."`. 75cd13f71 changed the shipped .unattended.conf.example to `GENERATED_INDEXES=""`.
confirmedFindings.fix: Assert that GENERATED_INDEXES="" survives the stamp unchanged. Keep GENERATED_INDEXES in STAMP_RE, and add a separate arm that stamps a conf whose GENERATED_INDEXES carries a {{MEMORY_TREE_DIR}} pair, asserting it resolves to ${TR_T}${MT_KIT}/gen_build_index.py.

confirmedFindings.claim: The hook's new behaviour has no arm. It now runs on every commit ahead of the MERGE_HEAD exit, probes for the kit and conf, blocks only on `rc = 1`, and announces and passes on any other exit code. unattended.test.sh calls `--check-commit` directly, and check-wiring.test.sh only byte-compares a stub commit-msg.
confirmedFindings.fix: Add an arm that installs .githooks/commit-msg in the fixture repo, makes a real `git commit` with a `Pass: <unit>` trailer that stages an undeclared path, and asserts the commit is refused. Add a control where the conf is absent and the commit lands.

confirmedFindings.claim: The fail-closed path of overlap placement has no arm. When the record's base does not resolve (dsposok=0), every graded pass is counted as overlapped and the `check 23 overlap unavailable` line is reported. No fixture sets an unresolvable base.
confirmedFindings.fix: Add an arm: bind the run, give it a single unit with a stray write, set `base:` to a sha absent from the clone, then assert `check 23 FAILED` and the `overlap unavailable` report line.

confirmedFindings.claim: Three of verb_check_commit's branches have no arm: the brief-row subtraction (read_brief_paths over the index), the gen-region-only subtraction (`check_gen_region_only "HEAD:$p" ":$p"` at 9761), and the refusal when the trailer names a unit with no open pass (9749). The AC3 arm covers only the run-state file and a conf-declared generated output.
confirmedFindings.fix: Extend the unattended.test.sh --check-commit block. Add a staged brief file with its `brief · item` row (expect rc 0), a README edit confined to a gen region (expect rc 0) with a control edit outside it (expect rc 1), and `Pass: ARCH-tRun-7` with no dispatch row (expect rc 1 and the 'no open dispatched pass' text).

confirmedFindings.claim: Selfcheck 6c's only arm stages a missing generator. Its other failure conditions are never staged: a path token outside {memory_root,map_root,kit}, an empty path, and a missing `why`.
confirmedFindings.fix: Add two staged breaks to the aWP-4 AC5 block in selftest.py: a `path = "{nope}/x"` row and a row with `why` removed. Assert each reds 6c and is green once restored.

confirmedFindings.claim: memory-tree declares two `{memory_root}/backlog` [[generated]] rows with no condition. The kit's default SHARED_RECORDS (`resolve_shared_records`) and the shipped `.unattended.conf.example` both put `memory/backlog` under SHARED_RECORDS, so every adopter that has memory-tree installed now names one path under both condition-3 keys.
confirmedFindings.fix: Add `when = ".memory-tree.conf:BACKLOG_MODE=builds"` to both backlog rows. Teach resolve_generated_indexes (and govkit 6c) to read the key from the named conf and skip the row unless it matches. Do NOT drop the rows: gov runs BACKLOG_MODE=builds with GENERATED_INDEXES="" and relies on them. Add an arm that loads every real kit descriptor with the default/example SHARED_RECORDS and asserts no overlap.

confirmedFindings.claim: `--check-commit` reads the staged set with porcelain `git diff --cached --name-only`, which applies rename detection (diff.renames defaults to true) and lists only a rename's destination. Check 23 at the close reads `git diff-tree --name-only -r`, which does no rename detection and lists both source and destination.
confirmedFindings.fix: Use `st=$(git diff --cached --no-renames --name-only)`, or `git diff-index --cached --name-only HEAD`, keeping newline separation for the existing `for p in $st` loop. Add an arm that stages a `git mv` out of an undeclared path into a declared one and expects rc 1 naming the source.

confirmedFindings.claim: Check 23's ambiguous-attribution test still reads the pass commit's SUBJECT (`git log -1 --format=%s`) and matches sibling unit ids in it, even when the commit carries a `Pass:` trailer. Spec 2 S2 says a trailered commit is attributed by its trailer alone and its subject is never read.
confirmedFindings.fix: For a commit with a `Pass:` trailer, build the ambiguity test from the trailer ids (e.g. via `log_attribution_tokens -1 "$dshit"`). Fall back to the subject only when no trailer is present.

confirmedFindings.claim: `--check-commit` reads the trailer and subject differently from the close. It matches `^Pass:` case-sensitively, while `pass_commit`/`log_attribution_tokens` use `%(trailers:key=Pass)`, which is case-insensitive. It takes the subject as the first non-blank line, while the close's `%s` joins the whole first paragraph.
confirmedFindings.fix: Match the trailer key case-insensitively (or read it with `git interpret-trailers --parse | awk 'tolower($0) ~ /^pass:/'`). Take the subject as the first paragraph joined, as `%s` does. Better still, derive both through the same tokeniser `log_attribution_tokens` uses.

confirmedFindings.claim: Once a pass has committed, `check_pass_open` reports its row closed. So `git commit --amend` of the pass commit, carrying its `Pass: <unit>` trailer, is refused with 'has no open dispatched pass … declare it first: --dispatch'.
confirmedFindings.fix: When HEAD is the unit's pass commit (or `pass_commit` returns HEAD), treat the row as open for a trailered commit and grade the staged set against it. Add an amend arm.

confirmedFindings.claim: A live record with neither a `run-branch` nor a `branch-ref` fact (`dsrb` empty) falls into the OTHER RUN branch. That branch prints that its counted writes are 'graded at its own close', but no checkout can ever bind an empty branch, so no close will grade them.
confirmedFindings.fix: When `dsrb` is empty, print a distinct line (e.g. `check 23 UNBOUND <run>: <n> counted, no run branch recorded, so no close binds it`) instead of the OTHER RUN claim, or fail it.

confirmedFindings.claim: Spec 3 S4/§5 say an absent kit is an ANNOUNCED skip. When `.unattended.conf` exists but `unattended.sh` is not found, the hook's probe loop matches nothing and the commit-time check is skipped silently.
confirmedFindings.fix: After the loop, if `.unattended.conf` exists and no kit was found, echo a one-line notice that the unattended commit-time check was skipped.

confirmedFindings.claim: Spec 4 §5 promises that check 23 prints the effective generated set on the report channel, and that the kit README describes the `[[generated]]` declaration. Neither was built: no reader reports the resolver's output, and the README diff adds only the hook line.
confirmedFindings.fix: Emit `report "check 23 generated outputs: $GENERATED_INDEXES"` at a point after report() is defined, for example at the head of check 23 next to DS_HEAD_REF, ideally noting for each pair whether it came from kit.toml or from the conf. Add a README paragraph covering the `[[generated]]` row keys (path, generator) and the {memory_root}/{map_root}/{kit} tokens.
